policy: No additional alert instance may be added to this allowlist after primary benchmark results are inspected (qualification_gates_v1.0.json version_history / amendment record). The evaluator recomputes this set at runtime from the frozen seed SMILES and HARD-FAILS if it disagrees with the file below, rather than silently trusting either value.
atom_index_note: matched_atom_indices are RDKit atom indices produced by re-parsing generated_from_seed_smiles with Chem.MolFromSmiles -- deterministic for a fixed RDKit version, since that string is itself a canonical SMILES. An RDKit upgrade that changes canonicalization or the Brenk pattern set would change these indices and correctly trip the runtime cross-check.

alerts.scope: unwanted functionality due to potential tox reasons or unfavourable pharmacokinetic properties
alerts.reference: Brenk R et al. Lessons Learnt from Assembling Screening Libraries for Drug Discovery for Neglected Diseases. ChemMedChem 3 (2008) 435-444. doi:10.1002/cmdc.200700139.

pains_check.implication: Per qualification_gates_v1.0.json Section 5, PAINS remains an absolute gate for this seed; no PAINS amendment is needed.

known_rdkit_limitation_worked_around.issue: FilterCatalogEntry.GetFilterMatches(mol) returns only the FIRST occurrence of a pattern per catalog entry, even when a molecule has multiple disjoint matches (verified directly on benzidine, Nc1ccccc1-c1ccc(N)cc1, which has two chemically separate anilines but reports one match).
known_rdkit_limitation_worked_around.workaround: decisionbench_dd_eval.chem_metrics.get_brenk_instances extracts each entry's underlying SMARTS query mol via the first FilterMatch's GetPattern() and re-runs mol.GetSubstructMatches(pattern, uniquify=True) directly, which correctly enumerates every occurrence.
known_rdkit_limitation_worked_around.relevance: Required for v1.2's instance-aware classification -- without this workaround, a candidate with two independent instances of an allowlisted alert type (e.g. Ambroxol's own aniline plus an unrelated second aniline) would silently look identical to a candidate with only the seed's own aniline.
